release_notes.title: Update and Codex fixes
release_notes.summary: A quick fix for updates that sometimes failed their safety check, plus Codex support.
added: PlazCode now finds Codex's chat box on chatgpt.com/codex.
fixed: Updates sometimes stopped with "Release signature or file verification failed" even though the download was fine. Security software scanning the new files could block the check for a moment; PlazCode now waits and checks again (up to three times) before giving up, and shows the real reason if it still fails.
PlazCode's own program check retries files that are briefly in use by another program, without relaxing any check.
notes: The update fix starts working from the update after this one; a failed update to 1.24.28 retries by itself every 40 minutes, or choose Update now.
Codex was checked on a test page with a Codex-like layout; it was not tried live.
Windows is unsigned and Mac is not notarized, as before; your computer may ask you to confirm opening it.

release_notes.title: Screenshots, approvals and update warnings
release_notes.summary: Improves screenshot display, remembers task approvals in Plan Mode, and makes mismatched app and extension versions clear.
improved: The desktop Updates page shows active browser extension versions. Known outdated versions stay red when a later check fails.
fixed: Screenshot previews render from image bytes instead of image URLs that AI sites can block. Unreadable image data shows an error.
Approve all for this task now applies to the same command in Plan Mode.
Creation previews explain missing app support, oversized requests and invalid responses instead of showing a JSON parsing error.
notes: Replacing only the EXE does not update an extension loaded from another folder. Use the full update and load the updated extension folder.
Real Studio captures and the reported creation-preview failure were not reproduced on the affected computer.
The Windows app is unsigned and the Mac app is not notarized.

release_notes.title: Fewer limit errors and lower usage
release_notes.summary: Fixes the "message exceeds your input limit" error that stopped Claude in the middle of normal work, and makes PlazCode use noticeably less of your AI plan.
improved: PlazCode uses less of your AI plan: the AI no longer has to look up each command before using it, Ultra mode no longer re-sends its whole skill pack with every request, and the extra reference PlazCode adds to a request is smaller.
When the AI saves a note to your vault, PlazCode no longer sends the whole vault summary straight back to it.
fixed: Claude (and other sites) stopped with "This message exceeds your 12000 character input limit" even after a normal prompt. The extra notes PlazCode adds now always fit your limit: they are shortened, or wait for the next message. Command results themselves are never cut.
notes: Your Input characters setting still works the same for everything you type.
The Windows app is unsigned and the Mac app is not notarized, as before. Your computer may ask you to confirm opening it.

release_notes.title: ClickUp Ask Brain connects again
release_notes.summary: Fixes Start Agent on ClickUp's Ask Brain, which used to stop right after the AI's first reply and never finish connecting. Nothing else changes.
fixed: Start Agent now finishes connecting in a new ClickUp Ask Brain chat. Before, PlazCode stopped about a second after Brain's first reply, the bar said "Not connected to this chat yet", and the rest of the setup was never sent.
Why it happened: ClickUp changes the page address as soon as a new chat gets its first message, and PlazCode took that for a different chat. It now treats it as the same chat.
Everything else is unchanged: other AI sites, ClickUp agent chats, and your settings, memory and connections.
notes: Tried on a real ClickUp Ask Brain chat in AgentScript mode: all five setup steps went through and PlazCode reported it was ready. Before the fix, the same test stopped after the first reply.
ClickUp agent chats and Firefox were not changed and were not tried on a live account. Automated tests on Windows, Mac and Linux must pass before this is published.
The Windows app is unsigned and the Mac app is not notarized, as in earlier versions. Your computer may ask you to confirm opening it.
